predecessors.name: Swedish Empire
predecessors.text: the metropole: Sweden, whose Africa Company (Carloff, first administrator) founded the colony on 22 April 1650

successors.name: Dutch Gold Coast
successors.text: Fort Carlsborg at Cape Coast, 'part of the Dutch Gold Coast' from April 1663

ledger.x: 1650 (22 April): the Swedish Gold Coast is founded at Cabo Corso.
1652: Fort Christiansborg is built at Osu, Accra.
1657: Fort William and Apollonia are lost.
ledger.cp: recipient not named on the page

ledger.x: 1658: Fort Christiansborg is captured by the Danes.

ledger.cp: recipient not named on the page

ledger.x: 1658 (27 January): Carloff returns with a Danish privateer and takes Fort Carlsborg.
1660 (10 December): Swedish administration returns to Fort Carlsborg.

wars.name: Danish-Swedish struggle for Cabo Corso
wars.outcome: Carloff retook Fort Carlsborg for the Danes on 27 January 1658; Samuel Schmidt sold the colony to the Dutch West India Company in April 1659; the Dutch occupied it March 1659 - December 1660; the Treaty of Copenhagen (1660) returned Cabo Corso to Swedish…

wars.name: Dutch capture of the Swedish Gold Coast
wars.outcome: Dutch victory: Fort Carlsborg and Fort Christiansborg seized on 20 (infobox 22) April 1663; Sweden formally relinquished the colony on 22 July 1667; the English seized the area on 9 May 1664.

certainty.note: Forts with their grounds, drawn as circles; the page gives no boundary for any.
